**Reasoning:**
The white cottony mycelium at the soil line is the most diagnostic feature. This is classic for **Southern Blight** (caused by *Sclerotium rolfsii*), which:
- Produces distinctive white mycelial fans at the stem base/soil line
- Causes crown and stem rot right at soil level
- Results in rapid whole-plant collapse/death
- Thrives in warm, sandy soils (consistent with the sandy substrate visible)

The longitudinally split stem also shows the internal stem rot damage characteristic of this disease. While Sclerotinia can look similar, the sandy soil, stem-base location, and growth pattern align most strongly with Southern Blight.
